SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / NATURE & WORKPLACE

Inspired by nature biophilic design for office walls.

Bring nature in with a plan for its care. This Space Craft planning note looks at inspired by nature biophilic design for office walls through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEChoose conditions before plantsThink beyond a green featureMake upkeep part of the designMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Choose conditions before plants

Assess daylight, watering access, available space and responsibility for maintenance. Match plant choices to the actual setting with help from an appropriate supplier.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Think beyond a green feature

Natural materials, views and access to daylight can form part of the same conversation. Keep circulation clear and consider the people who may have sensitivities to scent, pollen or maintenance products.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Make upkeep part of the design

Plan drainage, containers and cleaning before installation. A simple, well-maintained planting scheme may serve the workplace better than a complex feature with no clear owner.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Map daylight and maintenance access.
  • Assign responsibility for ongoing care.
  • Keep plants clear of work surfaces and escape routes.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
